Plots a cross wavelet scalogram

Source: R/plot_wavelet_coherence.R
plot_wavelet_coherence.Rd

Plot cross wavelet scalogram using the outcome of the analyse_wavelet_coherence function.

Usage

plot_wavelet_coherence(
  wavelet_coh = NULL,
  lowerPeriod = NULL,
  upperPeriod = NULL,
  n.levels = 100,
  palette_name = "viridis",
  color_brewer = "viridis",
  useRaster = TRUE,
  periodlab = "Period (metres)",
  x_lab = "depth (metres)",
  keep_editable = FALSE,
  dev_new = wr_dev_new_default(),
  plot_dir = TRUE,
  plot_arrows = TRUE,
  pwr_quant = 0.85,
  n_arrows = 75,
  T_unit = NULL,
  P_unit = NULL,
  arrow_length = 0.075,
  arrow_lwd = 1.9,
  arrow_angle = 25,
  add_lines = NULL,
  add_points = NULL,
  add_abline_h = NULL,
  add_abline_v = NULL,
  add_data = TRUE,
  add_avg = FALSE,
  plot_horizontal = TRUE,
  colour_brewer = NULL
)

Arguments

wavelet_coh

Wavelet coherence object to plot (required): the list returned by analyse_wavelet_coherence. Its Coherence, Phase, Period, x1/y1 and x2/y2 elements are used. Default=NULL.

lowerPeriod

Shortest period shown on the period axis, in the depth/time unit of the records (numeric, > 0). NULL uses the shortest period of wavelet_coh. Default=NULL.

upperPeriod

Longest period shown on the period axis, in the depth/time unit of the records (numeric, > lowerPeriod). NULL uses the longest period of wavelet_coh. Default=NULL.

n.levels

Number of colour levels of the coherence scale (integer, > 1); the breaks are quantiles of the coherence. Default=100.

palette_name

Name of the colour palette of the power (colour) scale, a character string. Which names are valid depends on color_brewer:

  • color_brewer = "grDevices": "rainbow", "heat.colors", "terrain.colors", "topo.colors", "cm.colors", or any of the 115 hcl.colors palettes (list them with grDevices::hcl.pals()), for example "viridis", "Plasma", "Inferno", "YlOrRd", "Spectral", "Blue-Red", "Zissou 1".

  • color_brewer = "viridis": "viridis", "magma", "inferno", "plasma", "cividis", "rocket", "mako", "turbo".

  • color_brewer = "RColorBrewer": "BrBG", "PiYG", "PRGn", "PuOr", "RdBu", "RdGy", "RdYlBu", "RdYlGn", "Spectral", "Accent", "Dark2", "Paired", "Pastel1", "Pastel2", "Set1", "Set2", "Set3", "Blues", "BuGn", "BuPu", "GnBu", "Greens", "Greys", "Oranges", "OrRd", "PuBu", "PuBuGn", "PuRd", "Purples", "RdPu", "Reds", "YlGn", "YlGnBu", "YlOrBr", "YlOrRd" (also listed by wr_brewer_palettes()).

  • color_brewer = "colorRamps": "blue2green", "blue2green2red", "blue2red", "blue2yellow", "cyan2yellow", "green2red", "magenta2green", "matlab.like", "matlab.like2", "ygobb".

  • color_brewer = "scico" (all except "batlowK" need the scico package): "acton", "bam", "bamako", "bamO", "batlow", "batlowK", "batlowW", "berlin", "bilbao", "broc", "brocO", "buda", "bukavu", "cork", "corkO", "davos", "devon", "fes", "glasgow", "grayC", "hawaii", "imola", "lajolla", "lapaz", "lipari", "lisbon", "managua", "navia", "nuuk", "oleron", "oslo", "roma", "romaO", "tofino", "tokyo", "turku", "vanimo", "vik", "vikO".

Low power is drawn with the first colour of the palette and high power with the last. Default="viridis".

color_brewer

Palette family from which palette_name is taken, a character string: "grDevices", "viridis", "RColorBrewer", "colorRamps" or "scico" (the last one, except for "batlowK", needs the scico package). See palette_name for the palette names of each family. Default="viridis".

useRaster

Draw the scalogram as a raster image (TRUE) or as a vector image of individual cells (FALSE) (logical). Vector images are slow to draw and give large files. Default=TRUE.

periodlab

Label of the period axis (character). Default="Period (metres)".

x_lab

Label of the depth/time axis (character). Default="depth (metres)".

keep_editable

Keep the graphical parameters (par, layout) of the plot after the function returns, so that extra elements can be added to the plot afterwards (logical). With FALSE the previous graphical parameters are restored on exit. Default=FALSE.

dev_new

Open a new plotting window for the plot. The wavelet plots contain a raster image that needs more room than the small RStudio plot pane, which gives "figure margins too large" errors or clipped text, so a separate window is opened by default in the RStudio GUI. In every other front end (plain R, ESS, Positron, knitr, Rscript) the plot is drawn on the current device and no window is opened. Set TRUE or FALSE to force either behaviour, or set options(waverider.dev_new = TRUE/FALSE). Logical. Default=wr_dev_new_default(): TRUE in the RStudio GUI, FALSE elsewhere.

plot_dir

Direction of the depth/time axis (logical): TRUE draws it with values increasing from left to right (or top to bottom in a vertical plot), FALSE reverses the axis. Default=TRUE.

plot_arrows

Draw phase arrows on the scalogram (logical). Arrows are drawn at the local coherence maxima along the period axis whose coherence is above the pwr_quant quantile; their direction gives the phase difference between the two records (pointing right: in phase, left: anti-phase). Default=TRUE.

pwr_quant

Quantile of the coherence (numeric, between 0 and 1) above which phase arrows are drawn; higher values give fewer arrows. Default=0.85.

n_arrows

Approximate number of arrow positions along the depth/time axis (integer, > 0); the columns of the scalogram are thinned to about this number. Default=75.

T_unit

Horizontal size of the arrows in depth/time units (numeric). NULL (or P_unit = NULL) uses an automatic, fixed visual length of 0.3 inch whatever the record length. Default=NULL.

P_unit

Vertical size of the arrows in log2 period units (numeric). NULL (or T_unit = NULL) uses the automatic size (see T_unit). Default=NULL.

arrow_length

Length of the edges of the arrow head, in inches (numeric; length of arrows). Default=0.075.

arrow_lwd

Line width of the arrows (numeric). Default=1.9.

arrow_angle

Angle between the shaft and the edges of the arrow head, in degrees (numeric; angle of arrows). Default=25.

add_lines

Lines to draw on the scalogram, e.g. tracked periods (matrix or data frame, or NULL for none): depth/time in column 1 and one or more columns of period values after it; each period column is drawn as a separate line. Default=NULL.

add_points

Points to draw on the scalogram (matrix or data frame, or NULL for none): depth/time in column 1 and one or more columns of period values after it. Default=NULL.

add_abline_h

Positions of extra horizontal lines (numeric vector, e.g. c(2, 3, 5), or NULL for none). In a horizontal plot these are periods; in a vertical plot (plot_horizontal = FALSE) they are depth/time values. Default=NULL.

add_abline_v

Positions of extra vertical lines (numeric vector or NULL for none). In a horizontal plot these are depth/time values; in a vertical plot they are periods. Default=NULL.

add_data

Draw the two data series in a panel next to the scalogram, the second one in red (logical). Default=TRUE.

add_avg

Draw the average coherence per period (Coh.avg) in a panel to the side of the scalogram (logical). Default=FALSE.

plot_horizontal

Orientation of the plot (logical): TRUE puts depth/time on the x-axis and period on the y-axis; FALSE draws a vertical plot with depth/time on the y-axis. Default=TRUE.

colour_brewer

British spelling of color_brewer, with the same options; if given (not NULL) it overrides color_brewer. Default=NULL.

Value

The output is a plot of a cross wavelet scalogram.

References

Roesch, A., & Schmidbauer, H. (2018). WaveletComp: Computational Wavelet Analysis. R package version 1.1. https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=WaveletComp

Moca, V. V., Bârzan, H., Nagy-Dăbâcan, A., & Mureșan, R. C. (2021). Time-frequency super-resolution with superlets. Nature Communications, 12(1), 337. doi:10.1038/s41467-020-20539-9

Author

plotting code based on the "wt.image" and "analyze.coherency" functions of the 'WaveletComp' R package

Examples

# \donttest{
#Example 1. A cross superlet plot of two etp solutions with noise overprint


etp_1 <- astrochron::etp(
 tmin = 0,
 tmax = 1500,
 dt = 1,
 eWt = 1.5,
 oWt = 0.75,
 pWt = 1,
 esinw = TRUE,
 standardize = TRUE,
 genplot = FALSE,
 verbose = FALSE
)

etp_2 <- astrochron::etp(
 tmin = 0,
 tmax = 1500,
 dt = 1,
 eWt = 1,
 oWt = 0.5,
 pWt = 1.5,
 esinw = TRUE,
 standardize = TRUE,
 genplot = FALSE,
verbose = FALSE
)

etp_1[, 2] <- etp_1[, 2] + wr_coloured_noise(
 nrow(etp_1),
 sd = sd(etp_1[, 2]) / 1.5,
 mean = mean(etp_1[, 2]),
 phi = 0.9
)
etp_2[, 2] <- etp_2[, 2] + wr_coloured_noise(
 nrow(etp_2),
 sd = sd(etp_2[, 2]) / 1.5,
 mean = mean(etp_2[, 2]),
 phi = 0.9
)

coh_etp <- analyse_wavelet_coherence(
 data_1 = etp_1,
 data_2  = etp_2,
 upperPeriod = 1024,
 lowerPeriod = 2
)
plot_wavelet_coherence(wavelet_coh = coh_etp, lowerPeriod = 2, upperPeriod = 1024,
              n.levels = 100, palette_name = "rainbow", color_brewer = "grDevices",
              useRaster = TRUE, periodlab = "Period (metres)", x_lab = "depth (metres)",
              keep_editable = FALSE, dev_new = TRUE, plot_dir = TRUE,
              plot_arrows = TRUE,
              pwr_quant = 0.85,
              n_arrows = 50,
              T_unit = NULL,
              P_unit  = NULL,
              arrow_length = 0.1,
              arrow_lwd = 2,
              arrow_angle = 25,add_lines = NULL, add_points = NULL, add_abline_h = NULL,
              add_abline_v = NULL, add_data = TRUE, add_avg = FALSE, plot_horizontal = TRUE)

# }
